humor.line: The old American Football League of the 1960s gave us the scoreboard clock, the two-point conversion and names on jerseys. Now we know who to blame.
A $5 monthly debit card fee from Bank of America in 2011 sent about 440,000 people to credit unions with $4.5 billion. Five dollars can start a stampede.
Pilgrims brought the first American doughnuts to New England, and they were tiny 'nuts' of dough they'd learned to make in Holland. Dough-nuts, in the most literal sense.
Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti, founders of the website How to be a Redhead, created it to help redheads love their hair. Ginger and proud of it.
Men who don't usually cook make dinner while everyone else stays out of the kitchen, unless there's an emergency. Check the smoke detector first.
Basketball's first game used a soccer ball, nine players per team and peach baskets nailed ten feet up. Slam dunks came later.
Ballpark nachos were invented by Sal and Margarita Manriquez, who sold them as 'Margarita's State Fair Nachos' at the Dallas State Fair in 1964. Margarita deserves a bigger sign.
The saxophone's B-flat and E-flat models were first designed for military bands. Smooth operators in formation.
A Fort Lauderdale attorney created it in 2001, and lawyer jokes are banned. We'll keep ours to ourselves.
You're supposed to get out in nature and find your way back without a compass, or just pick the three things you'd bring if marooned. Pick snacks, obviously.
Before paper, books were clay tablets and then papyrus made from reed stems. Talk about heavy reading.
The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt, who refused to shoot a bear on a 1902 hunting trip, which inspired a cartoon and then the first teddy bear. Bears sure owe him one.
Eleven-year-old Marcia Pepe of Hoboken played three Little League games in 1972, and in 1973 New Jersey became the first state to let girls play. One girl, one big win.
Dark chocolate has to be at least 35 percent cocoa solids, so this chocolate-and-almond day is the healthier cousin of the milk chocolate one in July. We're calling it health food.
The word 'notary' traces back to the shorthand Cicero's clerk developed to take down Cicero's speeches. Talk about job security.
Puns have been around since Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian and Mayan hieroglyphics. Dad jokes: officially ancient.
Thomas and Ruth Roy of Wellcat created it to celebrate the heavenly, homey smell of bold cooking, and they say don't forget the sauerkraut and garlic. Maybe open a window.
Dr. Seuss's Fox in Socks and Oh Say Can You Say? are full of tongue twisters, so they're perfect for today. Try it three times fast.
Cappuccino is named for the Capuchin friars, whose reddish-brown hooded robes matched the color of the coffee. Hoodie weather, in a cup.
In Minsk, pianist Nikolai Panok played for six hours without stopping for World Pianist Day, which Belarusian pianist Ivan Manko started in 2014. Hope someone brought snacks.
El Salvador's national dish, the pupusa, has ties to cooking tools found at a village buried by volcanic ash about 2,000 years ago. That's an old family recipe.
Early puddings were savory and sometimes cooked in an animal's stomach before sweet ones took over in the 17th century. Dessert has come a long way.
Carl Sagan's 1980 PBS series Cosmos became the most widely viewed PBS program of its time. Stellar ratings.
Fried chicken sandwiches caught on as a handheld way to eat fried chicken while keeping your hands clean. Napkins still recommended.
Greek yogurt is regular yogurt with the whey strained out, which makes it thicker and creamier. Yogurt with a firmer handshake.
Scrapple was created by the Pennsylvania Dutch, and one of its old names, 'pawnhaus,' means finely chopped. Breakfast with a mysterious name.
Area codes were devised by AT&T in the 1940s, and today is the excuse to call someone outside yours. Dial an old friend.
Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli, born in 1445, wrote the first book to include double-entry bookkeeping, and he's called the father of accounting. Everything finally added up.
The word 'cupcake' first showed up in 1828, and a cupcake-like dessert appeared in the cookbook American Cookery in 1796. Small cake, big history.
In 2009, New York City temporarily renamed the corner of West 64th Street and Broadway '123 Sesame Street' for the show's 40th anniversary. Now we know how to get there.
The sundae got its name because George Giffy, who owned a soda fountain in Manitowoc, Wisconsin, decided to serve it only on Sundays. Sunday never tasted so good.
Pocky was first going to be called 'chocotekku,' until the makers found the name was already trademarked. Sometimes a name mix-up works out.
Singles' Day started at Nanjing University in China in 1993, when four single guys in a dorm decided to make being single more exciting. A party of one, four times.
National Metal Day falls on 11/11 as a nod to the movie This Is Spinal Tap, where a guitarist brags his amps go up to 11 instead of 10. Turn it up to eleven.
Air Day marks the start of commercial air service between the Hawaiian Islands in 1929. Island hopping just took off.

national.line: A Missouri dog trainer's dog earned a Guinness World Record for hanging clothes pins on a line with her mouth. Now teach her to fold.
Missouri hospitals helped twin sisters begin a new chapter after a rare separation surgery. Now each one gets her own hug.
Michigan firefighters rescued a deer that fell into a partly drained backyard swimming pool and got trapped. That deer skipped the polar plunge.
A hairstylist says you can tell Gen Z from Millennial salon customers by the greeting: 'Hey girl' versus 'Hey queen.' Your generation is showing.

pride.label: Life Saving Award
pride.line: Tyler Blattel of Missouri Cooperage, Lebanon Fire Lt. Joe Gerber, Firefighters Adam Moppin, Nick Davis and Paul Shomo, Capt. Terry Saltzman, Mercy paramedic Louis Corbeil and EMT Jeremy Vinson received Life Saving Awards in Lebanon in October for saving a Missouri Cooperage worker after a cardiac event. Now that's a team effort.
Jackson Snyder is Lebanon's Yellowjacket of the Week. Plenty to buzz about.
pride.label: Yellowjacket of the Week
All-State Honors
pride.line: Bolivar freshman Brielyn Hines took seventh at state in golf for all-state honors, and tennis players Jillian Horner, Adelyn Seay and Kayla Goodman each finished fourth at state. Bolivar may need a bigger trophy case.

The Lake of the Ozarks Idiots Club has passed $2 million in help for local kids in poverty, with the milestone dollar buying clothes for a Macks Creek School student. Turns out these idiots are geniuses.
pride.label: $2 Million Milestone

pride.line: Julie Routh, a lifelong Bolivar resident and principal at Sherwood Elementary in Springfield, was named MOSHAPE Administrator of the Year for supporting health and physical education. Somebody earned an A in gym class.
pride.label: Administrator of the Year

pride.line: The Gasconade C-4 Wildcats won their last game of the season against Success. Ending on a high note.
pride.label: Season Finale Win

pride.line: Eye of the Storm Massage celebrated its grand opening with a Bolivar Area Chamber of Commerce ribbon cutting at 290 E. Broadway in October. Stress relief is officially open for business.
pride.label: Grand Opening

local.line: Heritage Bank of the Ozarks and the City of Lebanon are working together to find a new manufacturer for the Ice Cream Factory building. Here's hoping for a sweet ending.
Lebanon High School students performed Shakespeare's 'Much Ado About Nothing' last week. Finally, a teenager explaining Shakespeare to adults.
Chick-fil-A opens its first Osage Beach location today, Nov. 5. The Lake just got a lot more chicken.
Ameren is warning people not to dump leaves into Lake of the Ozarks, to protect water quality. The Lake is not a salad bowl.
Retired Polk County school staff toured the Ozarks Coca-Cola plant in Springfield on Oct. 20 and heard it began in 1911 in a basement on the Bolivar square. Pop history, literally.
Season 3 of 'Ozark Law' premiered Nov. 4 on A&E, back at Lake of the Ozarks. The Lake's reality career keeps going.

music.line: Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert and Cody Johnson are among the first performers named for the CMA Awards, live Nov. 18 on ABC with Lainey Wilson hosting solo. Set the DVR now.
Dolly Parton will get a special tribute at the 60th CMA Awards. Bring extra rhinestones.
CMA host Lainey Wilson joked she has a bedazzled broom ready in case Ella Langley sweeps the awards. Cleanup on aisle country.
Kaitlin Butts released a 34-minute mini-movie to spotlight her new album, 'Hello, Honky Tonk.' Popcorn pairs well with steel guitar.
Former NFL quarterback Duck Hodges says his buddies keep asking him to set them up with Ella Langley, thanks to his wife's friendship with her. Good luck, fellas.

weird.line: An emu on the loose in Connecticut was captured and reunited with its owner. Talk about a bird on the run.
A black bear paid a surprise visit outside a home near Santa Barbara, California. No reservation needed.
An alligator snuck into a North Carolina bagel shop and sent the owner scrambling, all caught on camera. Probably just wanted cream cheese.
A baby goat covered in cash was caught on video running between cars in Florida. Talk about a rich kid.
Scientists cracked the code on a treasure ship's padlock, solving a 400-year-old maritime mystery. Somebody finally found the combination.
A farmer grew the biggest pumpkin in Texas history. Pie for the whole state.
Backyard cameras in Austin, Texas, caught playful raccoons tugging on the tail of a skunk stopping for a drink. Somebody is braver than they look.
The Transformers-themed band the Cybertronic Spree performed a psychedelic cover of Black Sabbath's 'War Pigs.' Autobots, roll out the amps.
Legolas archery sliding is now a sport, inspired by the scene in The Two Towers where he surfs a shield down stairs firing arrows. Don't try this on your stairs.
An angler has broken a 76-year-old smallmouth bass record, and he says he was targeting big bass. It's no fish story.
A Florida man found out his SUV had been repossessed before he even made his first payment. That's a speedy repo.
Claude Moore's rubber band ball weighs 11,578 pounds and beat a record from 2008. Don't ask to borrow one.
A man with a hard childhood went viral building the tallest bicycle ever ridden, and now he holds a Guinness World Record. Getting off is the hard part.
Scientists say they discovered dinosaur blood in a 115-million-year-old fossil. Nobody tell Hollywood.
A mammoth fossil found in Acadiana is revealing Louisiana's Ice Age past. Imagine the size of that crawfish boil.
Fiji Airways set a new world record for the largest beach choir. Flight attendants finally got everyone's attention.
Abu Dhabi's Natural History Museum broke a Guinness World Record using 748,000 LEGO bricks. Barefoot visitors, beware.
